copy.title: WHY PEOPLE DISAPPEAR ON YOU

steps.why: before anyone ghosts, the brain runs a split-second price check on honesty.
the exit is always chosen at the exact moment friction becomes visible.

steps.rule: See silence as a decision, not an accident
steps.why: no reply is an active choice that felt cheaper than a hard sentence.

steps.rule: Stop reading it as rejection of you
steps.why: they are avoiding a conversation, not a person, and that changes what it means.

steps.rule: Respond to what they actually did
steps.why: treating avoidance as avoidance stops you chasing a problem that was never yours.

copy.kicker: Silence is cheaper than honesty for them
copy.thumb_scene: Wick stands facing camera on a plain white studio background, arms loose at his sides, holding a phone with a blank unanswered screen toward the lens, a single unopened message bubble visible on it, expression flat and clear-eyed.
copy.send_to: the friend still waiting on a reply they will never get
